nodes.label: Japanese / Irezumi
nodes.description: Te-bori tradition: bold outlines, flowing backgrounds (waves, wind bars), folklore motifs. Designed as one continuous composition across the body.

nodes.label: American Traditional
nodes.description: Old-school canon: heavy black outlines, limited bold palette, designs that hold for decades.

nodes.label: Blackwork
nodes.description: Solid black saturation and negative space; stipple to fully packed panels. Graphic, no color.

nodes.label: Fine Line
nodes.description: Single-needle precision: botanicals, script, jewelry-fine detail. Ages softly.

nodes.label: Neo-Traditional
nodes.description: Traditional bones with contemporary painterly depth and expressive color.

nodes.label: Realism / Portrait
nodes.description: Photographic portraiture built from hours of reference study; precise value control.

nodes.label: Dotwork
nodes.description: Sacred geometry and stippled texture built from thousands of individual dots.

nodes.label: Tribal / Polynesian
nodes.description: Bold angular patterns from Polynesian heritage, designed with cultural respect and fitted to anatomy.

nodes.label: Koi
nodes.description: The carp that swims upstream. Perseverance against the current; the dragon koi has completed its journey.

nodes.label: Chrysanthemum
nodes.description: Autumn flower of Japan, tied to the emperor and the sun. Perfection and rejuvenation.

nodes.label: Dragon
nodes.description: Water deity in Japanese lore: strength, wisdom, protection. Generous, not fire-breathing.

nodes.label: Hannya mask
nodes.description: The jealous woman of Noh theater transformed into a demon. The destructive power of obsession.

nodes.label: Waves (seigaiha)
nodes.description: Stylized overlapping waves — calm persistence, good fortune. Japanese background element.

nodes.label: Wind bars
nodes.description: Diagonal bars of wind that move and flow behind the main subject in Japanese compositions.

nodes.label: Tiger
nodes.description: Protection against evil spirits; power and unpredictability in Japanese lore.

nodes.label: Rose
nodes.description: Love, secrecy, and the balance of beauty and pain. The most repeated traditional motif.

nodes.label: Swallow
nodes.description: The returning bird — every swallow marks a journey survived. Loyalty and homecoming.

nodes.label: Dagger
nodes.description: Betrayal, sharp truth, or protection. Often paired with heart or rose.

nodes.label: Heart
nodes.description: Love, courage, devotion. Usually drawn with a banner in traditional work.

nodes.label: Skull
nodes.description: Memento mori — remember that you die. Acceptance of mortality.

nodes.label: Serpent
nodes.description: Transformation (shedding skin), danger, and healing. Blackwork and neo-traditional.

nodes.label: Tiger lily
nodes.description: Pride and wealth; paired with the hannya mask for an anger-versus-pride contrast.

nodes.label: Monstera leaf
nodes.description: Modern botanical favorite — growth, connection, tropical ease. Fine line work.

nodes.label: Mandala
nodes.description: Sacred geometry — the universe, wholeness, meditation. Dotwork technique.

nodes.label: Perseverance
nodes.description: Enduring hardship without giving up. Embodied by the koi swimming upstream.

nodes.label: Transformation
nodes.description: Change achieved through struggle: the dragon koi, the serpent's shed skin.

nodes.label: Protection
nodes.description: The tiger and dragon guard against evil; placement near the heart or on the back.

nodes.label: Love & devotion
nodes.description: Rose, heart, swallow — the traditional vocabulary of commitment and return.

nodes.label: Memento mori
nodes.description: Honest acceptance of mortality. The blackwork philosophy.

nodes.label: Heritage
nodes.description: Tribal patterns encode genealogy and identity, worn with cultural respect.

nodes.label: Healing
nodes.description: The serpent's shed, the chrysanthemum's bloom — and the studio's aftercare ritual.

nodes.label: Wholeness
nodes.description: The mandala — the self as a complete universe, meditated around the spine.

nodes.label: Homecoming
nodes.description: The swallow's return to land — journeys survived, promises kept.

nodes.label: Mara Voss
nodes.description: Founder. Twenty years behind the machine, te-bori apprenticeship in Osaka. Japanese / irezumi and blackwork; hand-poked sessions on request.

nodes.label: Jon Bell
nodes.description: Two-year traditional apprenticeship. American traditional, neo-traditional, dotwork. Heavy outlines, full-spectrum color packing.

nodes.label: Sofia Reyes
nodes.description: Ex-illustrator. Fine line botanical and realism / portrait. Single-needle control; quarterly bookings.

nodes.label: Forearm
nodes.description: High-visibility canvas; botanicals and traditional flash read well. Popular first tattoo.

nodes.label: Upper arm / shoulder
nodes.description: Classic first-piece placement; large enough for real composition.

nodes.label: Full sleeve
nodes.description: Shoulder to wrist, one continuous composition, 4–6 sessions. Japanese backgrounds must flow across the triceps.

nodes.label: Back
nodes.description: The largest canvas — 6–10 sessions. Traditional home of irezumi and memento-mori statements.

nodes.label: Chest
nodes.description: Visible, personal, closer to the heart. Mandalas and hannya masks sit well.

nodes.label: Ribs
nodes.description: High pain, private placement. Fine line and script work best.

nodes.label: Leg / thigh
nodes.description: Large surface, lower pain; good for larger motifs and geometric work.

nodes.label: Hand / fingers
nodes.description: High visibility, high wear, faster fade. A statement, not a starter piece.
